status: official named-access and legal-use evidence; never an exact-position or current-trail-conditions feed

policies.caution: Park maps and Ontario Trail Network geometries do not confirm signed intersection coordinates, winter road access, bridge passability, safe cliffs or current trail closures.

anchors.name: South Kabeyun Trailhead
anchors.approach: South on Ontario Highway 587, about 36.5 km south along the highway; the large lot is marked with a brown-and-yellow sign naming Kabeyun, Sawyer Bay, Ravine Lake and Sea Lion trails. Ontario Parks also describes it as roughly five minutes beyond Marie Louise Lake Campground.
anchors.roadKmReference: Ontario Parks says 36.5 km south on Highway 587; it does not specify an odometer zero-point suitable for GPS turn instructions.
anchors.visitorNote: Arrive early when demand is high. A valid day-use or other qualifying permit must be displayed. Verify today's road conditions and posted access before departure.

evidence.claim: Officially named large signed South Kabeyun parking lot and capacity limitations.
All three difficult Giant summit trips begin at the South Kabeyun trailhead; five-minute drive beyond campground.

anchors.name: Kabeyun / Sawyer Bay approach
anchors.visitorNote: Ontario Parks treats Sawyer Bay Trail as cycling-permitted and describes hiking routes that switch from it to a short Kabeyun connector; do not infer an exact junction pin.

evidence.claim: Head approach cycles along Sawyer Bay Trail and continues on a walking-only short Kabeyun connector.
Sawyer Bay Trail is on the official list of trails where cycling is permitted.

anchors.name: Kabeyun / Talus Lake junction
anchors.visitorNote: The legal bike cutoff for South Kabeyun is the Talus Lake junction. Ontario Parks describes a bike rack at the junction. The distances are round-trip trip components, not GPS segment geometry.

evidence.claim: Cycling permitted on South Kabeyun only as far as the Talus junction.
13.4 km round-trip bike / 8.4 km walk for Top of the Giant; rack at Kabeyun/Talus.

anchors.name: Sawyer Bay / Talus Lake walking connection
anchors.visitorNote: The published Nanabosho route rides Sawyer Bay and continues on Talus Lake Trail on foot. The exact turnoff location and any designated bike storage spot are not georeferenced here.

evidence.claim: Nanabosho trip splits cycling on Sawyer Bay from a walking-only Talus Lake and Nanabosho approach.

anchors.name: Talus Lake / Top of the Giant hiking approach
anchors.visitorNote: After leaving the bike at Kabeyun/Talus, proceed on foot via Talus and Top of the Giant as signed in the park. The exact junction position remains unverified.

evidence.claim: The Top of Giant itinerary is Kabeyun bike segment followed by Talus and Top of the Giant walking segment.

anchors.name: Sawyer Bay / Kabeyun / Head walking transition
anchors.visitorNote: Ontario Parks describes riding the Sawyer Bay approach, then walking the 0.6 km Kabeyun connector and 1.4 km Head Trail. No official rack is documented; exact stop coordinate is unverified.

evidence.claim: 12.2 km round-trip ride, 4 km round-trip walk; 0.6 km Kabeyun connector and 1.4 km Head Trail each way. No bike rack at transition.

anchors.name: Sawyer Bay / Talus / Nanabosho walking transition
anchors.visitorNote: Ontario Parks describes riding the first 5.5 km of Sawyer Bay Trail, then hiking the Talus and Nanabosho trails. No official rack is documented; exact stop coordinate is unverified.

evidence.claim: 17 km overall return: 11.8 km bike / 5.2 km walk. No bike rack at walking transition.
